title: Jonah and the Sigil
premise: Juniper Eriksen, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers who once kept the Thornfell passes, has spent years erasing herself from every ledger and memory. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she learns it bears the Sigil—a seal that can unbind the ancient oath-magic sleeping beneath the mountains, and the reason her order was hunted to extinction. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and courted by a rebel cell that wants the Sigil as a weapon, Juniper must decide whether justice means restoring the law that destroyed her people or breaking the seal forever. In the end, she speaks the final oath over her own name, dissolving the Sigil and her identity with it, so that no one—crown, rebel, or god—can ever wield what she was.
about_author: Mirabel Voss is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons mapping the passes she now populates with smugglers and ghosts. She writes fantasy about people the maps forgot, and swears every mountain in her books is real except the ones that matter most.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Names
chapters.summary: Juniper guides a salt caravan through the Thornfell passes, deliberately forgettable, trading on roads only she remembers. A flashback hints at the order of swordspeakers and their purge. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the loneliness of chosen invisibility, and the first tremor that it cannot last.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: At a river ford, Juniper finds a courier bleeding out among the stones, pursued by riders wearing no colors. He presses a wax-sealed map into her hands and gasps the word 'Sigil' before dying. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: dread—the moment invisibility ends and she becomes a target by possession alone.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Say
chapters.summary: Juniper studies the map in a smuggler's den; its markings match oath-script she was taught as a child but swore never to use again. The den's keeper, Brannoc, notices her recognition and quietly sends word to someone. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the past reaching for her through her own hands.

chapters.title: Riders in Grey
chapters.summary: Crown inquisitors arrive in the valley town asking after a dead courier and a woman 'who walks like a soldier.' Juniper watches an innkeeper she trusted lie badly for her. POV: Juniper, with a brief interlude from Inquisitor Hale's report. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve—she must move tonight.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers Her
chapters.summary: Fleeing through a pass she hasn't walked since childhood, Juniper finds the mountain itself responding to her presence—old wardstones flickering awake at her touch. She realizes the Sigil map leads to the Oathvault, heart of her order's power. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: grief and wonder entangled; the land never forgot her even when she begged it to.

chapters.title: The Rebel Who Owes Her Nothing
chapters.summary: Rebel scout Tam Vey intercepts Juniper, sent by Brannoc's message. He offers shelter with the Thornfell Compact, rebels who want the Sigil to break the Crown's claim on the mountains. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: wary attraction—he sees a weapon where she sees a wound.

chapters.title: The Compact's Bargain
chapters.summary: In the rebel hold of Dunmarrow, Compact leader Sera Ilves makes her case: the Sigil could free the mountain folk from Crown levies forever. Juniper refuses to hand it over and is detained 'for her protection.' POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the trap of good intentions—justice offered as a cage.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: An old Compact archivist deciphers the map's margin: the Sigil must be unbound—or destroyed—before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, or the oath-magic breaks loose uncontrolled. Six weeks remain. POV: Archivist Maren. Emotional beat: a clock starts ticking inside the story's bones.

chapters.title: Hale Descends
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Hale reaches Dunmarrow with a warrant and a memory-tithe: he carries a device that reads names out of minds. The Compact hides Juniper, but a young rebel is tithe-read and breaks. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: chilling competence—Hale believes he is the just one.

chapters.title: The Tithe of Names
chapters.summary: Interrogations begin; the broken rebel gives up Juniper's hiding place. Tam helps her escape through the flooded mine shafts against Sera's orders, earning her trust at the cost of his standing. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: gratitude complicated by guilt—her survival costs others their safety.

chapters.title: Oath-Script and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: On the high road, Juniper finally tells Tam what the swordspeakers were: not heroes, but enforcers of an oath that bound the mountain clans' memories to keep a greater war buried. POV: Juniper, framed as confession. Emotional beat: shame surfacing—she begins questioning whether destroying the Sigil serves justice or just her own peace.

chapters.title: The Village With No Yesterday
chapters.summary: They shelter in a village where, generations ago, the swordspeakers bound away a massacre from collective memory. An elder recognizes Juniper's stance, her cadence—and spits at her feet. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: horror at what her order's 'peace' actually purchased.

chapters.title: Sera's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Sera catches up with them, now willing to help Juniper reach the Oathvault—if Juniper will let the Compact decide the Sigil's fate afterward. Meanwhile Hale burns a Compact safehouse behind them. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance forged under pressure; everyone's motives are half-honest.

chapters.title: The Pass of Hanging Bells
chapters.summary: The party crosses a haunted pass where oath-bound bells still toll warnings. Hale ambushes them; Juniper, cornered, speaks her first oath in fifteen years and shatters his tithe-device, revealing herself fully. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: terrifying exhilaration—the power she renounced fits her hand like it never left.

chapters.title: What Speaking Costs
chapters.summary: Every spoken oath takes a memory as payment. Juniper wakes unable to recall her mother's face and conceals it from Tam, who suspects anyway. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: quiet devastation—heroism priced in selfhood, foreshadowing the ending's price.

chapters.title: The Vault Door
chapters.summary: They reach the Oathvault, sealed by a door that opens only to a living swordspeaker's full name spoken willingly. Juniper falters: speaking her true name aloud will make her findable by anyone who knows the old rites—including whatever sleeps below. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the threshold between hiding and claiming who she is.

chapters.title: Below the Seal
chapters.summary: Inside, they find the truth: the Sigil doesn't imprison an army—it holds the recorded oaths of thousands of conscripted mountain dead, whose bound voices fuel the Crown's legitimacy. Destroying it frees them; wielding it commands them. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—every faction's justice requires owning these voices.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Sera moves to seize the Sigil for the Compact, arguing the dead would choose freedom through rebellion's victory. Tam stands between them; Hale arrives with reinforcements, having tracked Juniper's spoken name. Three-way standoff in the vault. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: betrayal without villains—each side genuinely believes it acts for the wronged.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: The moon completes its turn as the vault begins to crack. Juniper realizes no faction can be trusted with the dead's voices—not the Crown, not the Compact, not herself. She begins the Unbinding Oath, which requires the speaker's entire remembered life as payment. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: terrible clarity and surrender.

chapters.title: Every Name She Ever Was
chapters.summary: Climax. As Hale's forces breach the vault, Juniper speaks the Unbinding, giving up her memories one by one—childhood, order, name—while the bound dead rise as voices, witness their own history aloud, and disperse free. Hale, hearing the full record of his Crown's crimes, lowers his sword. POV: Juniper, fragmenting. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-erasure done as gift, not escape.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Ford
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the Sigil is dust, the vault collapsed, the Compact and Crown forced into negotiation by the revealed truth. A woman with no past guides caravans through the Thornfell, feeling unaccountable grief at certain bends in the road. Tam leaves a carved token at the ford each season. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope—identity given away, yet somehow witnessed.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Epilogue. The elder from the memoryless village, now keeping a new honest record of the massacre, names the freed dead in a yearly reading—and includes one name no one recognizes: Jonah, the courier who started everything, revealed as the last other swordspeaker who chose death over capture to bring her the map. The book closes on Juniper, pausing at the sound of his name, almost remembering. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure—memory survives as story, carried by strangers.
